cost.callsOutsideATask: Calls outside a task (a connection test, for example) are not results.

auto.completedRanToAn: Completed ÷ ran to an end of their own (completed + failed + interrupted). What waits for you or is still running is not in the denominator: it has no result yet. For “filling in the form”, completed means that this run got the application submitted; a task that found the application already sent and did nothing counts neither as a success nor as a failure. This is the success rate of tasks, not what came of the applications: for that, see “Outcomes”.
auto.failedTheTaskStopped: Failed = the task stopped on an error of its own; interrupted = the app was closed during the task.
auto.byTheDayA: By the day a task started (local time). Click a legend entry to leave a series out.
auto.groupedByReasonMost: Grouped by reason, most frequent first
auto.durationIsTheMedian: Duration is the median of tasks that finished or failed; AI cost is everything spent on that kind of task (failed runs included) over the ones that succeeded.
auto.theFiguresAboveCount: The figures above count runs; one application can take several (waiting for your answer, for your sign-in, going on after a budget). Here the runs of one application are taken together. Only applications that have come to a result are counted: one that waits for your answer or sign-in, or is still being worked, is in no denominator.
auto.applicationsBroughtToWhere: Applications brought to where one press sends them (or sent) ÷ (those + the ones that failed). Failed: the agent said it could not, it stopped at the same place several times, or the task ended in an error.
auto.ofThePreparedApplications: Of the prepared applications, those that got there without a question to you, without being stopped by you and without getting stuck. A sign-in only you can make is not counted.
auto.sentWithEvidenceOf: Submitted with proof, of those to be submitted
auto.ofTheApplicationsYou: Of the applications you approved, or that the agent sent itself under “Submit when nothing is open”: those that are out with the confirmation page's words or a confirmation email kept. Those still on their way are not counted.
auto.allRunsOfOne: All runs of one application together; only the prepared ones are counted.
auto.fromEachApplicationsOwn: From each application's own record of its runs. An application often takes several: waiting for your answer or sign-in, sending after approval, going on after being cut off. Every run after the first opens the browser again, finds its way back to the form and checks what the last one filled - that is "going over it again".
auto.toolCallsOfEvery: Tool calls of every run after the first ÷ all tool calls. Lower is better: applications mostly done in one run, or taken up again without starting over.

accounts.secureTitle: How passwords and sessions are kept
accounts.securePassword: Kept in the credential manager of the computer AutoApply runs on (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain or the desktop keyring). It is read and sent to this page only when you press Show password, and hidden again after 30 seconds.
accounts.securePasswordFile: This computer has no usable credential manager, so passwords are kept in an encrypted file in the data folder (secrets.bin); whoever can read its master key can decrypt it. The database only records whether there is one; backups do not contain passwords. On a sign-in form the app types it itself and the AI does not see it. It is read and sent to this page only when you press Show password, and hidden again after 30 seconds.
accounts.secureSession: The cookies saved after a sign-in are kept encrypted in the data folder (sessions). For a site signed in to with this computer’s Chrome or Edge, that browser’s profile in the data folder (profiles) holds them too. Sessions are not in the database, and are in a backup only when you choose to include them.
accounts.secureProviders: Only the session is saved, never these accounts’ passwords.
accounts.secureLeaves: A password is typed only into a password box on the site it belongs to. A session leaves the data folder only in a file you export with Move a session (encrypted with the passphrase you choose), or in a backup you choose to include sessions in.

accounts.sessionHelp: The cookies saved after a sign-in. Not checked with the site: “Expires by” is an upper bound, and the site may end the session earlier.

about.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
about.diagnosticsHint: Copies the version, the build, how it runs, Python, the system, the data folder and where updates stand as plain text, for an issue report. No account, key or setting other than the update ones is included.
about.preparingHow: Installing what it needs; this can take a few minutes. The running version is not touched.
about.switchingHow: The tray app restarts AutoApply once what is in progress is done. This page reconnects when the new version is up.

fact.pendingHow: The tray app starts this release the next time it restarts AutoApply.
fact.whenIdleHow: Asked for from a notification: it switches the next time nothing is in progress, whatever the mode and the hours.

about.privacyShort: Checking only asks GitHub for its list of releases; nothing about you is sent.
about.idleHow: Idle means that nothing is applying or queued, nothing waits for you in a kept window, and no remote window is open.

byHand.title: Manual update
byHand.source: This copy runs from source and is updated by hand.
byHand.container: This copy runs in a container and is updated by pulling a new image.

risk.download: New versions are downloaded and prepared in the background, with their dependencies and browser, in the data folder: this uses network and disk space. The running version does not change until you switch.
risk.auto: AutoApply also restarts into a new version by itself, without asking: within the switch window, when nothing is in progress. If the new version does not start, the current one keeps running; the version before is kept so you can roll back.
